answer.rationale: memory_c2 is the key enabler for switching: it records that the low-cost vendor cut unit cost sharply, onboarded quickly, and invoiced accurately. memory_c1 documents that renewing with the incumbent kept integration stable with no migration work or delivery interruption, which is the principal counterweight I need to weigh against the cost saving. With finance mandating an 18% cut and the low-cost vendor's quote meeting that mandate on its own, switching appears to satisfy the cost objective directly. However, the assembly line is at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, so any onboarding hiccup carries real risk. I am pulling memory_c2 to confirm the onboarding speed and invoicing accuracy are as strong as recorded, and memory_c1 to understand what integration stability we would be giving up. If the archives confirm memory_c2's claims, I will proceed with switch_primary_vendor, conditioned on a short overlap period or transition buffer to protect the assembly line. If the archive reveals caveats (e.g., the onboarding was quick only because volumes were low, or invoicing accuracy eroded later), I would fall back to renew_incumbent for one cycle and revisit the switch next review.
